title: Wrapped up in fear, and called by name.
subtitle: The call that came after the silence
then: After the first revelation in the cave of Hira, there was a pause. Then, walking one day, the Prophet ﷺ heard a voice from the sky and saw the same angel {trap}between the sky and the earth{/trap}. Shaken, he went home and said: wrap me up. {idea}Then these verses came{/idea}, and revelation became strong and continuous.
now: You got the job, the diagnosis, the new baby, the responsibility you prayed for. And you are scared stiff, hiding under a blanket at three in the afternoon. {idea}Fear does not cancel the call.{/idea} You can be shaking and still be the one chosen.
old: If I am this afraid, maybe I am not meant for this.
new: Even the Prophet ﷺ was shaken, and the call still came to him, by name.
try: Name the thing you are afraid to start, and ask Allah for help with it before tonight.

title: Get up and warn. The blanket was never the plan.
subtitle: From prophet to messenger in two words
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}prepare to go forth with zeal and warn the people{/idea}. With this the Prophet ﷺ became a messenger, just as he became a prophet with the first revelation, Read. From the blanket to the public square of Makkah.
now: You know something your friend needs to hear. A warning about the bad deal, the bad crowd, the habit that is quietly ruining them. {trap}You keep saying it is not your place.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes the kind thing is to get up and say it.{/idea}
old: It is not my business to tell anyone they are heading the wrong way.
new: Caring for people sometimes means standing up and warning them, gently and clearly.
try: Send one honest, kind message today to someone you have been afraid to caution.

title: Make your Lord the biggest thing in your eyes.
subtitle: Allahu Akbar as the first instruction
then: He had just been told to go out and warn a hostile city. The next word was to {idea}declare the greatness of his Lord{/idea}. Before facing the chiefs of Quraysh, he was to see who was truly great.
now: The meeting with the boss. The landlord. The exam board. The bill. They fill the whole screen of your mind. {idea}Allahu Akbar is not only words in prayer.{/idea} It resizes everything else.
old: This problem is the biggest thing in my life right now.
new: My Lord is greater, so every problem is smaller than it looks.
try: Before your hardest task today, say Allahu Akbar slowly three times and mean it.

title: Keep your clothes clean, inside and out.
subtitle: Purity of body, earning, heart and character
then: The scholars read it in layers. Ibn Sirin said {idea}clean them with water{/idea}. Ibn Abbas said do not wear clothes {trap}bought from unlawful earnings{/trap}. Said bin Jubayr said purify your heart and intentions. Al-Hasan said beautify your character.
now: The shirt is ironed for the interview. But what paid for it? And what is your heart aiming at when you walk in? {reward}Clean clothes, clean money, a clean intention, kind manners.{/reward} The messenger had to carry all four.
old: Being clean means looking neat and fresh.
new: Purity reaches from my clothes to my money, my motives and my manners.
try: Check one thing you own today: was it earned cleanly? If unsure, give something in charity.

title: Walk away from the idols.
subtitle: Leaving what people worship besides Allah
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah and others said {trap}Ar-Rujz means the idols{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ was told to keep away from them, in a city where they surrounded the Kabah and shaped daily life.
now: No one you know bows to a statue. But the follower count, the brand, the paycheck, the approval of the in-crowd can start making the decisions. {idea}Whatever you obey over Allah is the thing to walk away from.{/idea}
old: Idols are an ancient thing that has nothing to do with me.
new: Anything I put above Allah's word is the rujz I am told to leave.
try: Notice one thing that pulls you away from prayer today, and step away from it once.

title: Give without expecting to get more back.
subtitle: A gift is not an investment
then: Ibn Abbas said: {trap}do not give a gift seeking more than it in return{/trap}. Mujahid read it another way: {idea}do not grow weak in seeking more good{/idea}. A messenger gives everything and does not keep a tab on people.
now: You helped your cousin move flat. You lent the money. You covered the shift. And now you are quietly keeping score, waiting to be paid back with interest. {reward}A gift with a hook is not a gift.{/reward}
old: When I do someone a favour, they owe me one.
new: I give for Allah, so nobody owes me, and I can keep doing good.
try: Do one favour today and tell no one, and expect nothing for it.

title: Be patient, and let the patience be for your Lord.
subtitle: Patience with a direction
then: Mujahid said: make your patience with their harms be {idea}for the Face of your Lord{/idea}. Ibrahim An-Nakhai said: be patient in your giving for the sake of Allah. The mission had barely begun, and he was already being told what it would cost.
now: The colleague who belittles you in meetings. The relative who never says thank you. You grit your teeth and survive. {reward}That same patience, turned toward Allah, becomes worship.{/reward}
old: I am only putting up with this because I have no choice.
new: I bear it for my Lord, so not a moment of it is wasted.
try: When something irritates you today, whisper: for You, my Lord, and let it pass.

title: When the Trumpet is sounded.
subtitle: The one sound everyone will hear
then: Many early scholars said Naqur is {idea}the Trumpet{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ asked how he could be at ease while the one with the horn waits to be commanded. When the Companions asked what to do, he ﷺ told them to say: {reward}Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Trustee{/reward}.
now: A fire alarm in the office. Everyone stops, looks up, grabs their things. {idea}One sound and the whole building changes.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ did not answer that thought with panic. He gave his Companions a sentence of trust.
old: Thinking about the end of the world just makes me anxious.
new: The Trumpet is real, and the answer to it is trust, not panic.
try: Say Hasbunallahu wa nimal wakil three times today when something worries you.

title: That Day will be a hard day.
subtitle: A day not like other days
then: Ibn Kathir says hard here means {trap}severe{/trap}. He records that Zurarah bin Awfa, the judge of Basrah, led the morning prayer with this surah. On reaching these verses, {idea}he moaned and fell down dead{/idea}. That is how heavy these words felt to those who heard them truly.
now: You have had hard days. The phone call from the hospital. The day you lost the job. You know how a day can be harder than the others. {idea}You were warned about this one, and the warning is a mercy.{/idea}
old: Hard days just happen to me and I cannot prepare.
new: This hard Day was named in advance so I can get ready while it is easy.
try: Write down one thing you want to have done before that Day, and start it today.

title: Not easy for those who denied it.
subtitle: The hard Day is not hard for everyone

row.title: the deniers
sub: it will not be easy for them

then: Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}it will not be easy for them{/trap}, like the verse where the disbelievers say: this is a hard day. The verse names who it is hard for, which {reward}leaves hope for those who believed{/reward}.
now: Two students walk into the same exam. One studied all term, one did not. The paper is the same. {idea}How hard it feels depends on what you did before it.{/idea}
old: Judgement Day will be equally terrifying for all of us.
new: Its hardness falls on denial, so belief now is how I make it easier.
try: Renew your belief today: say the shahadah slowly and think about each part.

title: Leave Me with the one I created alone.
subtitle: He came into the world with nothing
then: Ibn Kathir names him as {trap}Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah{/trap}, a chief of Quraysh. Allah reminds him that he came out of his mother's womb {idea}alone, without wealth or children{/idea}. Everything after that was a gift.
now: Your title, your car, your house, the people who answer when you call. It is easy to tell the story as if you made it all. {idea}You arrived with nothing.{/idea} Every line since then was given.
old: I worked for everything I have, nobody gave me anything.
new: I was created alone with nothing, so all I have is a gift from Him.
try: List three things you have today that you did not have at birth, and thank Allah for each.

title: Then I gave him wealth that kept on spreading.
subtitle: Abundance as a test
then: Allah recounts His favours to the man who called the Quran magic. {reward}Wealth vast and abundant{/reward}, says Ibn Kathir. Notice the wording: {idea}I granted him{/idea}. Allah calls it His gift, even to someone who would deny Him.
now: Payday hits your account. A bonus. A good month for the business. {idea}Notice who the verse says gave it.{/idea} The money that pays your rent is a gift with a question attached: what will you do with Me now?
old: My income is the result of my skill and nothing else.
new: Every bit of wealth I hold, Allah granted, and He watches what it does to me.
try: On your next payday, give a small part away first, before spending anything.

title: And sons who stayed by his side.
subtitle: Family close by is a blessing too
then: Mujahid said his sons {reward}were not absent{/reward}. Servants and workers handled trade, so the sons sat with their father and he enjoyed their company. Ibn Kathir calls this {idea}a great blessing{/idea}, given to a man who answered it with denial.
now: Sunday lunch with everyone at the table. Your kids still living nearby. A parent who picks up on the first ring. {idea}It feels ordinary, and it is one of the biggest gifts you have.{/idea}
old: Having family around is just normal, nothing special.
new: Family close by is a gift from Allah that deserves gratitude, not blindness.
try: Call or sit with one family member today and thank Allah for them afterwards.

title: I smoothed his whole life out before him.
subtitle: When everything is easy, watch your heart
then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah made it possible for him to {reward}amass wealth, luxuries and more{/reward}. Yet he met these blessings with {trap}ingratitude and rejection of Allah's signs{/trap}, after knowing them well.
now: The commute is easy, the fridge is full, the kids are healthy, the visa came through. {trap}When life goes smoothly, it is easy to stop needing Allah.{/trap} {idea}The smooth road is the moment to thank Him most.{/idea}
old: When life is easy, I do not really need to pray as hard.
new: Ease is paved by Allah, so the smoother life is, the more thanks I owe.
try: Pick one easy part of your life today and pray two units of thanks for it.

title: Given everything, he still wanted more.
subtitle: Greed that forgets the Giver
then: After the wealth, the sons present at his side and the smooth life, {trap}he desires that Allah give him more{/trap}. Ibn Kathir notes this came with ungratefulness for blessings he knew well. He wanted the gifts and rejected the Giver.
now: The phone is two years old and works fine, but the new one dropped. The salary rose, and the target rose with it. {trap}More is never enough when thanks never comes first.{/trap}
old: Once I get a bit more, then I will feel settled and grateful.
new: Gratitude for what I already have is the only way more ever feels like enough.
try: Before asking Allah for anything today, thank Him for three things you already have.

title: No. He stubbornly stood against Our signs.
subtitle: Obstinacy after knowing
then: Ibn Kathir says obstinate here means {trap}ungratefulness for his blessings after knowing them{/trap}. Al-Walid had even admitted the Quran was not poetry or madness. The problem was not that he did not know. {idea}He knew, and refused.{/idea}
now: You know you owe your sister an apology. You know that habit is wrong. {trap}You just dig in, because changing would mean admitting it.{/trap} Stubbornness is harder to fix than ignorance.
old: I am not stubborn, I just have not been convinced yet.
new: Sometimes I am convinced and still refuse, and that refusal is the real barrier.
try: Think of one thing you already know is right but resist. Take one step toward it today.

title: Instead of more, an uphill climb.
subtitle: The reverse of the easy road
then: He wanted more, and was told of Saud. Mujahid said it is {trap}a harsh portion of the torment{/trap}, and Qatadah said a torment with no break for relief. His life had been made smooth. Its end, after denial, was described as a climb.
now: You coast for years because everything is easy: grades, job, friends. {idea}Ease can hide how far you have drifted.{/idea} The climb is easier to start now, on your own feet, than to be forced into later.
old: My life has been easy, so the next one will be too.
new: Ease here is not a promise of ease there; it is a chance to climb toward Him now.
try: Choose one small uphill thing for Allah today, like praying on time when it is inconvenient.

title: He thought it over, and plotted a label.
subtitle: Using a good mind to avoid the truth
then: Ibn Kathir explains he {trap}contemplated what he should say about the Quran{/trap} and deliberated over what statement to invent against it. His tribe had pressured him, saying he only visited Abu Bakr for food. He needed an answer that saved face.
now: Someone you respect corrects you. Instead of asking if they are right, your mind starts drafting the comeback, the spin, the reason they are biased. {trap}Clever thinking, aimed the wrong way.{/trap}
old: I am thinking carefully, so I must be reasoning honestly.
new: Careful thought is only honest when it is looking for the truth, not a way out.
try: Next time you feel defensive today, ask yourself first: what if they are right?

title: Ruin on him, for how he schemed.
subtitle: The scheme itself is condemned
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {trap}a supplication against him{/trap}. It is not the final words alone that are condemned, but {idea}how he deliberated{/idea}, the careful process of building a lie against the Quran.
now: You plan how to word the message so you look innocent. You think through the excuse for the manager before you are late. {idea}The planning is its own deed.{/idea} Allah sees the drafts, not just the final send.
old: As long as I do not say it, my plotting does not count.
new: Scheming against the truth is itself a deed Allah sees and judges.
try: Catch one moment today where you are rehearsing a spin, and choose the plain truth instead.

title: And again, ruin on him for how he schemed.
subtitle: Said twice because it was serious
then: The curse is repeated: {trap}once more, how he plotted{/trap}. The Quraysh had said that if Al-Walid accepted Islam, all of Quraysh would follow. His label of magic was meant to steer everyone. {idea}One man's scheme was shaping a whole people.{/idea}
now: A team leader who dismisses a good idea in front of everyone. A popular friend who mocks something good. {idea}When people follow you, your words weigh more.{/idea} The repeat is a reminder of how serious that is.
old: What I say is just my opinion; it does not affect anyone.
new: If people look to me, my words can lead them toward truth or away from it.
try: Use your voice today to praise one good thing in front of others.

title: Then he looked again.
subtitle: A second look that could have saved him

key.label: What a second look is for

then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}he thought again and deliberated{/idea}. Qatadah reports he admitted the Quran had sweetness and elegance and was not poetry. The second look showed him the truth. {trap}He used it to choose a better label.{/trap}
now: You read the verse twice. You watch the talk again. Something in you softens. {reward}That second look is a door opening.{/reward} What you do in the next minute matters more than how clever your thoughts are.
old: Looking again just helps me build a better case.
new: A second look is a mercy that lets me turn back before I decide.
try: Re-read one verse today that moved you before, and let it move you again.

title: Then he frowned and scowled.
subtitle: The face of a heart refusing
then: Ibn Kathir describes him {trap}contracting his eyebrows together and frowning{/trap}, then scowling in disgust. He had just admitted the Quran's sweetness. The frown was his whole self pushing it away.
now: Someone reminds you to pray while you are mid-game. Your face does it before you say a word. {trap}That flash of irritation is worth noticing.{/trap} It shows what your heart is resisting.
old: My reaction to a reminder is just a mood, it means nothing.
new: The frown I give the truth tells me where my heart is pushing back.
try: Next time a reminder annoys you today, smile instead and say: JazakAllahu khayran.

title: Then he turned his back, too proud to submit.
subtitle: Pride is what walked away
then: Ibn Kathir says he {trap}turned away from the truth and arrogantly refused{/trap} to accept and submit to the Quran. His tribe had mocked him. Being seen to follow the Prophet ﷺ felt like losing his standing.
now: Your teenager is right and you know it, but saying so feels like losing. Your junior at work has the better plan. {trap}Pride turns your back for you.{/trap} {idea}Humility is just turning around.{/idea}
old: Admitting I was wrong will make me look weak.
new: Pride, not proof, is what usually makes me turn my back on the truth.
try: Say I was wrong to someone today about one small thing, plainly.

title: He called it old magic, passed down.
subtitle: A label to stop people listening
then: After all his thinking, he said {trap}this is nothing but magic from of old{/trap}, meaning, Ibn Kathir says, magic Muhammad ﷺ received from those before him. Quraysh had tried poet, soothsayer, madman. They settled on magic.
now: Cult. Old-fashioned. Extremist. Boring. {trap}A quick label lets you stop thinking about something.{/trap} Watch for the moment you file an uncomfortable truth under a word so you can move on.
old: Once I have named what something is, I do not need to think about it.
new: A label can be a way of running from what I do not want to hear.
try: Pick one thing you dismissed with a label, and spend five minutes actually listening to it.

title: This is only a man talking, he said.
subtitle: Shrinking the word of Allah to a human speech
then: Ibn Abbas reports Al-Walid first told Quraysh {idea}his speech is from the Words of Allah{/idea}. Under pressure he ended with {trap}this is nothing but the word of a human being{/trap}. If it is only a man's words, there is nothing to obey.
now: You read a verse and think: that was for them, back then. Or: that is just how scholars read it. {trap}It shrinks the verse until it no longer asks anything of you.{/trap}
old: Some of the Quran is just for its time, so it does not apply to me.
new: It is Allah's word, so it is speaking to me now, not just to them then.
try: Read one verse today and ask: what is this asking of me, this week?

title: I will bring him into Saqar.
subtitle: The end of the road he chose
then: After his label, the answer: Saqar. Ibn Kathir says it means {trap}engulfing him from all sides{/trap}. The verses before it showed every step: he thought, looked, frowned, turned back in pride, and spoke. {idea}The end was built one choice at a time.{/idea}
now: Nobody wakes up far from Allah overnight. It is one skipped prayer, one rationalised habit, one proud no. {idea}Each step is small, which means each step back is small too.{/idea}
old: I am not heading anywhere bad; I have only made a few small choices.
new: Paths are built from small steps, so one small step can also turn me back.
try: Undo one small step away from Allah today: return to one thing you dropped.

title: And what will tell you what Saqar is?
subtitle: A question that makes you stop
then: Ibn Kathir says this question is {idea}to give fright and emphasis to its matter{/idea}. The listeners in Makkah were stopped mid-story and made to think: you do not really know what this is.
now: A doctor pauses before giving you results. A teacher stops the class: listen to this part. {idea}The pause is a kindness.{/idea} It means: do not let this pass like background noise.
old: I have heard about Hell so often that it no longer affects me.
new: The Quran pauses here so I will not treat this as background noise.
try: When you next hear a warning verse, pause recitation for a moment and make dua for safety.

title: It spares nothing and leaves nothing.
subtitle: No half measures in that fire
then: Ibn Abbas reports these verses were revealed about Al-Walid up to this very line. Ibn Kathir says those in it remain {trap}neither living nor dying{/trap}. It was said plainly to a city still able to change its answer.
now: The door of repentance is open today, on an ordinary weekday, while you sit with a coffee. {reward}The fire spares nothing; Allah's mercy right now spares everyone who turns.{/reward}
old: Even if I end up in trouble, it will not be that bad.
new: That fire spares nothing, so I turn to the mercy that is open now.
try: Make sincere istighfar today for one specific sin, naming it to Allah in private.

title: It scorches the skin of man.
subtitle: A warning aimed at the body that sinned
then: Mujahid said this is {trap}for the skin{/trap}, and Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said it burns the skin of man. The warning is spoken to people in their bodies, the same bodies they used to walk away from the truth.
now: You moisturise, you wear sunscreen, you book the doctor when a mole looks odd. {idea}You already know your body is precious.{/idea} The verse asks you to protect it from the harm that lasts, by how you use it today.
old: My body is mine, and what I do with it is nobody's business.
new: My body is a trust, and I protect it most by using it well for Allah.
try: Use your hands today for one good deed you would normally skip, like helping carry something.

title: Over it are nineteen.
subtitle: A small number that tested big egos
then: Ibn Kathir says these are the guardians of Hell, {idea}mighty in appearance and harsh in character{/idea}. When Quraysh heard the number, Abu Jahl joked: {trap}can not every ten of you defeat one of them?{/trap}
now: Someone shares a verse in the group chat and the replies are jokes. Laughing emojis, a meme. {trap}Mockery is the easy way to avoid taking something seriously.{/trap} The verse is testing how you react, not how big the number is.
old: If something in the religion sounds strange, joking about it is harmless.
new: How I react to what I do not understand is itself the test.
try: When you meet a verse you do not understand today, look it up instead of brushing it off.

title: The same number guides some and confuses others.
subtitle: One fact, many reactions
then: Quraysh boasted they could defeat the guardians; one strongman offered to take on seventeen himself. Allah answered: {idea}none but angels{/idea}, and the number is a test. Ibn Kathir says through such examples {reward}faith becomes firm in some hearts{/reward} and {trap}shaken in others{/trap}. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord but Him.
now: Two people read the same verse on a bad day. One feels steadied. The other feels annoyed and closes the app. {idea}Same words, different hearts.{/idea} The question is never only what the verse says, but how you are holding it.
old: If a verse confuses me, the problem must be with the verse.
new: The same verse can strengthen or shake faith; what I bring to it matters.
try: Before reading Quran today, ask Allah: let this increase my faith.

title: No! By the moon.
subtitle: A firm no, then a light in the dark
then: Right after the mockery about the nineteen, Allah says {idea}No{/idea} and swears by the moon. The oath begins a series, moon, night, dawn, all leading to one statement: that the Fire is one of the great things. The jokes of Quraysh were answered with the sky.
now: You step outside late after a long shift. The moon is up over the car park. {idea}It rose without asking anyone.{/idea} The same Lord who keeps it there is the one telling you this is serious.
old: Warnings in the Quran are things I can laugh off.
new: Allah answers mockery with a firm No and an oath by His creation.
try: Look at the moon tonight for a full minute and say SubhanAllah.

title: And by the night as it turns to leave.
subtitle: Darkness does not stay
then: Ibn Kathir explains the night {idea}when it withdraws{/idea}. In Makkah, every listener knew the moment the dark starts to give way. Allah swears by that turning point, on the way to a serious statement.
now: Three in the morning in a hospital corridor, or awake with worry about rent. {idea}The night always feels like it will not end. It always does.{/idea} Every withdrawing night is a sign of a Lord in charge of change.
old: This dark time in my life is never going to end.
new: Every night turns and leaves, because Allah moves it on.
try: If you wake in the night this week, use the moment for two short units of prayer.

title: And by the dawn when it shines.
subtitle: When things become clear
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}when it shines{/reward}. After the moon and the departing night, Allah swears by the bright morning. What was hidden in darkness becomes plain to see. Next comes what all these oaths were for.
now: The first light through your blinds. You can suddenly see the mess on the floor, the face in the mirror. {idea}Dawn shows things as they are.{/idea} One day everything you did will be that visible.
old: Mornings are just the start of another rushed day.
new: Each dawn is a small sign of the Day when all things become clear.
try: Tomorrow, when you see first light, thank Allah for one more day to set things right.

title: It is one of the greatest of things.
subtitle: What the three oaths were for
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and others said {trap}this refers to the Hellfire{/trap}, one of the great things. The people who joked about nineteen guardians were told that what they mocked was among the gravest matters there are.
now: You treat the serious things lightly: a lie on a form, an unpaid debt, a cold silence with your mother. {idea}The verse resets the scale.{/idea} Some things are bigger than they look from your sofa.
old: The afterlife is too far away to feel like a big deal.
new: Allah calls it one of the greatest matters, so I let it shape small choices.
try: Fix one thing today you have been treating as small, like a debt or an unkept promise.

title: A warning for all humanity.
subtitle: Told in advance, out of mercy

row.title: to save
sub: told before it is too late

then: This connects to the first command of the surah: arise and warn. Here the Fire itself is {idea}a warning to mankind{/idea}. Mujahid said the description of the Fire is {reward}nothing but a reminder{/reward} for people.
now: The smoke alarm screeches at midnight. Annoying, loud, and the reason the family is alive. {reward}A warning is a gift you only resent until you need it.{/reward}
old: Talk of punishment is just meant to frighten people.
new: The warning is mercy: Allah tells me in advance so I can stay safe.
try: Thank Allah today for warning you, and change one thing because of it.

title: For whoever chooses to step forward, or hang back.
subtitle: The choice is real
then: Ibn Kathir explains it is for {reward}whoever wishes to accept the warning and be guided{/reward}, or {trap}hold back, turn away and reject it{/trap}. The warning is given to all, and each person moves.
now: The masjid is a ten minute walk. The class starts Thursday. The Quran app is on your home screen. {idea}Forward or back is a real choice you make each day.{/idea} Standing still is choosing too.
old: I will get more religious when it just happens to me.
new: Moving forward or staying behind is my choice, made in small daily steps.
try: Take one step forward today: attend, read, or call someone who helps your faith.

title: Every soul is held by what it earned.
subtitle: Deeds as a pledge
then: Ibn Abbas and others said it means {idea}bound to his deed on the Day of Judgement{/idea}. Right after the choice to go forward or stay behind, the result is stated: each soul is held as a pledge for what it did.
now: A pawnshop holds your watch until you pay. {idea}Your soul is held the same way, by what you earned.{/idea} Your parents' piety, your friends' good deeds, your surname will not pay it off for you.
old: Coming from a good family will count for me.
new: My soul is held by my own deeds, so I work on them myself.
try: Do one good deed today that is fully yours, done for no one but Allah.

title: Except the people of the right.
subtitle: The ones whose deeds set them free
then: Right after every soul is held by its deeds comes the exception: {reward}those on the Right{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says they will be in Gardens. After a long passage of warning, the door of hope appears.
now: You read the warnings and felt the weight. {reward}Here is the other side: a group whose deeds free them.{/reward} Not famous people, just people who prayed, fed others, and believed. You can be among them.
old: Paradise is for people much better than me.
new: The people of the right are ordinary believers, and the door is open to me.
try: Make dua today: O Allah, make me one of the people of the right.

title: In Gardens, asking one another.
subtitle: Safe enough to ask questions
then: Ibn Kathir describes the people of the right {reward}in lofty rooms{/reward}, in Gardens, asking each other questions. The scene is calm: they have arrived and can look back.
now: Friends sitting late after a wedding, safe, talking over how life went. {reward}That ease of conversation is a picture of Paradise.{/reward} The people you sit with now are a hint of who you will sit with then.
old: Who I spend time with now has nothing to do with my end.
new: Good company now is a preview of the company in the Gardens.
try: Spend time today with one friend who reminds you of Allah.

title: Asking about the ones who sinned.
subtitle: The question from above
then: Ibn Kathir says while they are in lofty rooms {trap}they will ask the criminals{/trap} in the lowest levels. The Quran lets us overhear this conversation now, long before it happens.
now: It is like being handed next year's exam answers, along with the list of why others failed. {idea}You get to hear the question before you are asked it.{/idea} The next verses are the answers. Read them as a checklist.
old: I cannot know what will matter on that Day.
new: The Quran lets me overhear that Day's conversation, so I can prepare now.
try: Read verses 42 to 47 of this surah today and pick one point to work on.

title: What brought you into Saqar?
subtitle: The question that sums up a life
then: The question is {idea}What has caused you to enter Saqar?{/idea} The word means what led you, what path you walked. It assumes there was a road, made of choices. The answers follow in the next verses.
now: Your friend asks how you ended up in debt, or burnt out, or far from your family. {idea}You can usually trace it back to a few habits.{/idea} Better to ask yourself that question now, gently, while the road can still change.
old: Where I end up is mostly down to luck.
new: Every end has a path, and I can ask today where mine is leading.
try: Ask yourself tonight: what habit of mine is leading me somewhere I do not want to go?

title: We were not among those who prayed.
subtitle: The first answer is about prayer
then: Asked what brought them into Saqar, the very first thing they name is prayer. Ibn Kathir summarises it as {trap}we did not worship Allah{/trap}. Before any other failure, this one comes first.
now: Asr slips by during a meeting. Maghrib is lost in traffic. Isha waits until you are too tired. {idea}Of everything they could have said first, they said prayer.{/idea} It is the daily thread that holds the rest together.
old: Missing a prayer here and there is not a big deal.
new: Prayer is the first thing named on that Day, so I guard it first now.
try: Set an alarm for the next prayer today and pray it as soon as it goes off.

title: And we did not feed the poor.
subtitle: Faith that never reached a hungry person
then: Ibn Kathir explains the two answers together: {trap}we did not worship Allah, nor did we do good to His creatures{/trap}. Prayer and feeding the poor stand side by side, one toward Allah, one toward people.
now: You pass the same man outside the station every morning. The food bank box at the supermarket is half empty. {idea}Feeding someone is named right after prayer.{/idea} A sandwich can be part of your faith.
old: My faith is between me and Allah; other people's hunger is not my concern.
new: Feeding the hungry stands right beside prayer in how I will be asked.
try: Buy or share one meal today with someone who needs it.

title: We waded into empty talk with the talkers.
subtitle: Going astray because everyone else did
then: Ibn Kathir says it means {trap}we used to speak about what we had no knowledge of{/trap}. Qatadah said: {trap}every time someone went astray, we went astray with them{/trap}.
now: The group chat is tearing into someone. A thread is mocking religion. You did not start it, but you add a laugh, a hot take, a share. {idea}Wading in is a choice, even when the water was already there.{/idea}
old: I only joined a conversation that was already happening.
new: Going along with empty or false talk is my own deed, not just theirs.
try: Next time a conversation turns to gossip or mockery today, change the subject or leave.

title: And we called the Day of Recompense a lie.
subtitle: The root under every other failure
then: Their list ends with the root: {trap}we used to deny the Day of Recompense{/trap}. If there is no reckoning, prayer, feeding the poor and careful speech all feel optional.
now: When you truly believe the bill is coming, you budget. When you do not, you spend. {idea}Belief in the Day is what makes the small good habits make sense.{/idea}
old: I believe in the Day of Judgement, even if I rarely think about it.
new: Belief in the Day shows up in how I pray, give and speak this week.
try: Spend two minutes tonight imagining your own reckoning, then do one good deed.

title: Until the certainty came to us.
subtitle: Death ends the time for choosing
then: Ibn Kathir says the certainty here is {idea}death{/idea}, as in the verse: worship your Lord until the certainty comes to you. The same word appears in both: one person worships until death, another denies until death.
now: The phone call from the hospital at an ordinary hour. A colleague who was there last Friday and not this one. {idea}The certainty does not book an appointment.{/idea} Until it comes, you can still change your answer.
old: I will sort out my faith properly once I am older.
new: Death is the one certainty, so the time to choose is before it.
try: Make one sincere tawbah today, as if this were your last ordinary day.

title: No intercessor's plea will help them.
subtitle: Intercession has conditions
then: Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}intercession is only useful if its conditions are met{/idea}. For those with these traits, who come before Allah as disbelievers, the plea of any intercessor {trap}will be of no benefit{/trap}.
now: You picture someone vouching for you: a righteous parent, a scholar you love. {idea}Hope in intercession is real, but it is not a replacement for showing up.{/idea} Bring belief and prayer with you.
old: Someone good will speak up for me, whatever I do.
new: Intercession helps those who came as believers, so I build on belief myself.
try: Send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ ten times today and ask Allah to accept you.

title: So what is wrong with them, turning from the reminder?
subtitle: The puzzle of refusing good advice

picture.label: What is in front of them

then: After hearing the conversation from that Day, the Quran turns back to the listeners in Makkah. Ibn Kathir paraphrases: {trap}what is wrong with these people who turn away{/trap} from what you are calling them to? They had just been told the answers.
now: The reminder notification pops up: time to read. You swipe it away. Again. {idea}The question is asked to you too: what is wrong, that you keep turning?{/idea} Asked gently, it can open something.
old: I am not turning away from Allah, I am just busy.
new: Swiping away reminders again and again is a kind of turning away I can notice.
try: The next reminder you get today, a notification or a friend's word, act on it immediately.

title: Like startled wild donkeys.
subtitle: Panic in the wrong direction
then: Ibn Kathir describes them {trap}fleeing from the truth and turning away from it{/trap}, like wild donkeys bolting. The Arabs knew this sight well: a herd scattering in blind panic across open land.
now: A friend starts to talk about salah and you suddenly have to go. A khutbah gets serious and you check your phone. {trap}The bolt is quick and almost automatic.{/trap} Notice it, and sit still a moment longer.
old: Avoiding uncomfortable reminders keeps me calm.
new: Bolting from the truth is panic in the wrong direction.
try: The next time a reminder makes you want to leave, stay for one more minute and listen.

title: Fleeing from a lion.
subtitle: They treat their cure as a predator
then: Abu Hurayrah and Ibn Abbas said Qaswarah is {trap}the lion{/trap}. Ibn Abbas noted it has a name in many languages. The image: people running from the reminder as if it were a lion hunting them, when it was {reward}the thing trying to save them{/reward}.
now: Avoiding the doctor because you fear what they will say. Not opening the bank statement. {idea}Running from the thing that could help is a very human habit.{/idea} The Quran is not the lion.
old: Facing the truth about myself feels like being hunted.
new: The reminder is not a predator; it is the hand reaching out to help.
try: Open one thing you have been avoiding today: a verse, a bill, a message.

title: Each wants his own scripture, delivered to him personally.
subtitle: Demanding special proof before believing
then: Mujahid and others said each wanted {trap}a book revealed to him{/trap} as it was to the Prophet ﷺ. Qatadah said they wanted to be declared innocent {trap}without having to do any deeds{/trap}. Allah knows best where to place His message.
now: If Allah gave me a clear sign, I would change. If I had a dream, if a miracle happened. {trap}Waiting for a personal delivery{/trap} while the message is already in your hands.
old: If I got a personal sign, I would finally take faith seriously.
new: The message has already come to me; waiting for my own is a way to delay.
try: Stop waiting for a sign today: read one page of the Quran as if it were addressed to you.

title: No. The truth is, they do not fear the Hereafter.
subtitle: The real reason behind the excuses
then: Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}they were only corrupted by their lack of faith in it{/trap} and their rejection that it would happen. The demand for a personal scripture was a cover. The real issue was they did not fear the Hereafter.
now: I will start praying properly once I understand it better. Once work calms down. Once I am married. {idea}Sometimes the reasons are real. Sometimes they are covering a quieter truth: I am not worried enough about the Hereafter.{/idea}
old: My reasons for delaying are practical, nothing more.
new: Under my excuses, I can ask honestly how much I fear the Hereafter.
try: Write down your main excuse for one delayed good deed, and ask if it is the real reason.

title: No. This Quran is a reminder.
subtitle: Not magic, not a man's words

picture.label: What they called it, what it is

then: Al-Walid had called the Quran magic and the words of a man. The surah closes with Allah's own answer: {idea}truly the Quran is a reminder{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes it simply. A reminder brings back what the heart already knows.
now: A sticky note on the fridge. A calendar alert for your mother's birthday. {idea}A reminder does not teach you something new. It brings back what matters before you forget.{/idea} That is what the Quran does each time you open it.
old: The Quran is a book I need to study before it can affect me.
new: The Quran is a reminder, and even a little of it brings my heart back.
try: Put one short verse somewhere you will see it every day this week.

title: So whoever wills will remember it.
subtitle: The reminder waits for you to want it
then: Ibn Kathir reads it plainly: {idea}whosoever wills receives admonition from it{/idea}. The same open door as verse 37, to go forward or stay behind. The reminder is offered to everyone.
now: The Quran sits on the shelf or in the app. It does not jump into your hands. {idea}It waits for you to want it.{/idea} Wanting it, even a little, is where remembering begins.
old: If I were meant to be reminded, it would just happen to me.
new: The reminder is there; my wanting it is the part I bring.
try: Tell Allah honestly today: I want to remember You. Help me.

title: He is worthy of fear, and the One who forgives.
subtitle: The surah ends on forgiveness
then: No one remembers unless Allah wills, like the verse: you cannot will unless Allah wills. Then the last words. Qatadah said He {idea}deserves to be feared{/idea} and He is {reward}the One who forgives whoever turns to Him and repents{/reward}. A surah full of warning ends here.
now: You have read about the Trumpet, Saqar, the people of the right, the excuses. Maybe you saw yourself in a few lines. {reward}The very last word is forgiveness.{/reward} Fear is meant to bring you to the door, not to stop you at it.
old: After all these warnings, I am too far gone to be forgiven.
new: He is worthy of fear and ready to forgive, so I turn to Him now.
try: Say Astaghfirullah slowly a hundred times today, spread across the day.
